atoms.definition: Train on digit images with contiguous pixel blocks removed.
Fit separate RBF-SVM classifiers on transformed or augmented training features.
Weight classifier predictions by held-out validation decision margins.

molecule.mechanism: Structured block dropout forces the classifier to learn features robust to contiguous occlusion rather than salt-and-pepper noise alone, better matching realistic corruption patterns. Running three candidate pipelines in parallel on the same stratified split and weighting their test-time predictions by validation decision-function margin exploits the observation that higher-margin classifiers tend to generalize better under distribution shift. The margin weight replaces the fictional backward causality: instead of retroactively rewriting training, the winning configuration's margin score simply scales its contribution to the ensemble vote. No temporal paradox is required; the mechanism is a post-hoc weighted combination.
assumptions: Impossible assumption replaced: backward causality, where a future result modifies past initialization, is physically impossible. It is replaced by prospective parallel evaluation followed by margin-weighted ensembling, which is entirely feasible within the time budget. Lateral memory across simultaneous strands is replaced by ordinary sequential result logging. Strand-death margin amplification is replaced by proportional margin-based vote weighting derived from validation decision-function scores.
molecule.falsifiable_prediction: If structured block dropout augmentation does not outperform random pixel dropout on the corrupted test conditions, or if margin-weighted ensembling does not improve over the single best individual pipeline selected by validation accuracy alone, the intervention fails. Ablation: replacing margin weights with uniform weights should degrade mean corrupted accuracy if margin weighting is doing real work.
